theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Shanique must cut forty pieces of 50 × 50 × 5 mm angle square and to the same length. Which power tool is best for this job?
options: A 115 mm angle grinder with a thin cutting disc
A cold saw or bandsaw with a length stop
A jigsaw fitted with a fine metal-cutting blade
A portable drill with a hole saw attachment

questions.stem: Before handing out portable power tools to your team, what should you check first on each one?
options: That it has been used recently by someone else
That the casing is the same colour as the others
That the box and the manual are with the tool
Its test tag is in date and the cable is sound

questions.stem: Why is a residual current device (RCD) used with portable power tools?
options: It cuts the power fast if current leaks to earth
It keeps the tool running at a steady speed
It stops the cable overheating on a long run
It lets the tool run on both 110 V and 220 V

questions.stem: A 220 V tool is plugged into an extension lead rated for less current than the tool takes. What is the main risk?
options: The tool will run faster than it should
The disc will spin the wrong way
The lead can overheat and start a fire
The RCD will stop working altogether

questions.stem: Many Jamaican workshops have both 110 V and 220 V outlets. What must you check before plugging in a power tool?
options: The distance from the outlet to the bench
The colour of the plug top
The voltage on the tool's rating plate
The age of the extension lead

questions.stem: A grinder runs at 11 000 rpm. A disc of the right size is marked with a maximum of 13 300 rpm. Can it be fitted?
options: Yes, its rated speed is above the grinder's
No, the disc must match the speed exactly
No, a faster-rated disc will wear too fast
Yes, but only with the guard removed

questions.stem: Why must a 230 mm disc never be fitted to a 115 mm angle grinder, even with the guard taken off?
options: It would make the cut too wide for steel
It would be too heavy for the side handle
It would cut too slowly to be any use
Its rim would spin faster than it is rated

questions.stem: What is kickback on an angle grinder?
options: The grinder slowing down when you push it too hard
The disc snagging and throwing the tool back
Sparks bouncing back off the work
The motor stopping when it overheats

questions.stem: How should the guard on an angle grinder be set when cutting?
options: Between the disc and you, so sparks go away
Removed, so you can see the cut line
Turned towards the work to cover the cut
Loosened, so it can move with the disc

questions.stem: Which disc should be used on an angle grinder to remove a weld cap and blend it flush?
options: A 1 mm thin cutting disc
A wire cup brush
A grinding or flap disc
A diamond tile blade

questions.stem: A resin-bonded grinding disc has been kept in a damp container for a long time. What should you do?
options: Dry it in the sun, then use it as normal
Check its date and state; if in doubt, scrap it
Use it only for light grinding work
Soak it in oil so that it does not crack

questions.stem: Why must the safety chain or strap be fitted when a magnetic base drill is used on the side of a beam?
options: To stop the cable being pulled out of the plug
To hold the cutter in the arbor during use
To earth the drill to the beam for safety
To hold the drill if the magnet lets go

questions.stem: Why should you not use a magnetic base drill on a beam while someone is arc welding on the same beam?
options: The sparks will blunt the cutter's teeth quickly
The drill will run too slowly
The beam will be too hot to drill
Weld current may flow through the drill

questions.stem: Why does a magnetic base drill hold less well on thin plate, or on paint and mill scale?
options: Thin plate bends too much under the drill
It needs clean, thick enough steel to grip
The drill motor runs too fast on thin plate
Paint and scale make the motor overheat

questions.stem: Using N = (1000 × V) ÷ (π × D), find the spindle speed for a 12 mm HSS drill in mild steel at a cutting speed V of 25 m/min.
options: 2083 rpm
300 rpm
663 rpm
6631 rpm

questions.stem: A 20 mm hole and a 6 mm hole are drilled in the same steel with HSS drills. Which is right?
options: The 20 mm drill runs at a slower speed
Both drills run at the same speed
The 20 mm drill runs at a faster speed
Speed does not matter with HSS drills

questions.stem: When drilling stainless steel, why is a steady, firm feed used rather than a very light one?
options: A light feed blunts the chuck jaws
A light feed lets the steel work-harden
A light feed makes the drill motor run hotter
A firm feed stops the RCD from tripping

questions.stem: What often happens when a twist drill breaks through thin sheet that is only held by hand?
options: It can grab the sheet and spin it round
It slows down and stops cutting at once
It gets blunt in one turn
It makes the hole undersize

questions.stem: Why should compressed air never be used to blow dust off your clothes or skin?
options: It wastes air that the tools need
It makes the compressor run too hot
It spreads the dust to other workers
Air can be forced into skin or eyes

questions.stem: What is a whip check (safety cable) across an air hose coupling for?
options: To keep the hose clean inside
To raise the air pressure at the tool
To stop the hose lashing if it parts
To lock the tool so it cannot be stolen

questions.stem: Before changing the cutter on an air-powered die grinder, what must you do?
options: Shut off the air, bleed it and unplug the hose
Hold the trigger down while you change it
Turn the regulator up so the tool runs freely
Point the tool at the floor and pull the cutter

questions.stem: Why should lithium-ion tool batteries be charged only on the maker's charger, in a cool, dry place?
options: So the battery's colour does not fade
So that the charger stays under warranty
A wrong charge can make them catch fire
So the battery weighs less when charged

questions.stem: A cordless drill battery is swollen and warm after a fall. What should you do?
options: Charge it straight away to cool it down
Take it out of use and report it
Tape it up and carry on, then charge it later
Put it in water so that it cannot catch fire

questions.stem: Grinding steel at the Centre is very loud. Which is the right rule for hearing protection?
options: Only the person grinding needs protection
Cotton wool in the ears is good enough
Hearing protection is needed only after an hour
Everyone in the noisy area wears it

questions.stem: Odane uses a needle scaler and a grinder for most of the day. What can long use of vibrating tools cause?
options: Burns to the skin of the palms
Better grip and stronger hands
Numb, tingling or white fingers
Eye strain and headaches

questions.stem: Which is a good way to reduce a worker's exposure to vibration from power tools?
options: Hold the tool tighter so it shakes less
Use blunt discs so the tool runs slower
Work through breaks to finish sooner
Rotate tasks and use low-vibration tools

questions.stem: Before cutting with a grinder near the timber roof of a shed in Mandeville, what must be done?
options: Remove what can burn and keep an extinguisher
Wet the steel so that no sparks are made
Work faster so the sparks have no time to land
Open the doors so the sparks blow outside

questions.stem: Cutting or grinding galvanised or painted steel gives off fumes. Which control is best?
options: Hold your breath during each cut
Local extraction and a suitable respirator
Wear a cotton bandana over your mouth
Work with the shop doors closed

questions.stem: Which tool is best for cutting a 300 mm round opening in 1.2 mm sheet steel for a duct?
options: An angle grinder with a 1 mm disc
A nibbler, started from a drilled hole
A hammer and a cold chisel
A magnetic drill with a 300 mm cutter

questions.stem: A trainee wants to use a 230 mm grinder to cut a small bolt in a tight corner. What should you advise?
options: Use a smaller tool that suits the space
Remove the guard so that the disc fits
Hold the grinder with one hand to reach
Use the grinder, but run it at half speed

questions.stem: A grinder's switch has been locked on with its lock-on button. What is the danger if the power fails and then comes back?
options: It will run in reverse when power returns
It cannot be turned off again
The disc will fall off the spindle
It may start up again by itself

questions.stem: What is the spindle lock button on an angle grinder for?
options: To bring the disc to a fast stop after cutting
To lock the switch on for long cuts
To hold the spindle while you change discs
To set the speed of the grinder

questions.stem: A corded drill sparks heavily inside its vents and has lost power. What is a likely cause for a competent repairer to check?
options: The chuck key has been left in
The drill bit is too sharp
The cable is too long for the drill
Worn carbon brushes in the motor

questions.stem: Why should the Centre keep a register of its power tools with their test dates and repairs?
options: To make sure each tool is used the same amount
To show each tool has been checked and is safe
To decide who may take tools home at night
To keep the tools in order of their colour

questions.stem: A grinder's cable has a cut in its outer sheath close to the plug. What is the right action?
options: Tag it out for repair by a competent person
Wrap the cut with insulating tape and use it
Cut the cable shorter and refit the plug yourself
Use it only with an RCD until it is fixed

questions.stem: How should a corded power tool be cleaned at the end of a job?
options: Wash it under a tap to remove the dust
Spray the motor vents with oil
Unplug it, brush out the vents and wipe it
Leave it dusty; it will be used tomorrow

questions.stem: Why are power tools kept in a dry, locked store in Jamaica's humid, salty air?
options: Damp causes rust and electrical faults
Tools work better if kept cool and dark
Dry tools need no inspection at all
Locked tools never need cleaning

questions.stem: You see a team member using a grinder without its side handle, to save time. What should you do?
options: Ignore it if they are experienced
Wait until the end of the day to say something
Take the grinder home to fix it
Stop them, fit the handle and explain why

questions.stem: Before a job with power tools on a building site in Spanish Town, what should be done first?
options: Hand out the tools and start
Check the site and do a risk assessment
Buy new tools for the job
Ask the client to stay close by to watch

questions.stem: How should the cable of a power tool be run across a workshop?
options: Across the walkway, so it is short
Through a doorway, under the door
Along a wall, or under a cable cover
Through a puddle, if the plug is dry

questions.stem: A new worker has never used a magnetic base drill. What is the best way to start them?
options: Let them read the label and try it alone
Show them, watch them use it, then sign off
Let them watch once from across the shop
Give them the oldest drill so it does not matter

questions.stem: A team member says his drill gave him a small electric shock. What must happen?
options: Stop, unplug it, tag it out and report it
Carry on, but wear rubber gloves
Put tape over the casing and continue
Swap the bit and try it again

questions.stem: Why is a wire wheel on a grinder a particular hazard to the eyes and skin?
options: It throws sparks further than a disc
It makes the grinder run faster
Wires can break off and fly out
It makes the steel too hot to touch

questions.stem: Why do some grinders have a variable speed setting?
options: So a bigger disc can be fitted on it
So that the guard can be taken off
So it can run on both 110 V and 220 V
To suit the speed to the disc and work

questions.stem: At the end of the day, what should a team leader check before the power tools go back to the store?
options: That each tool is still warm
That each one is clean, undamaged and logged in
That the cables are wound tightly round the tool body
That every disc has been taken off and thrown away

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

What is the frequency of the mains supply in Jamaica, in hertz (Hz)?

essays.stem: You are planning a job to cut, drill and grind steel brackets on site at a school in May Pen. Explain how you would choose the power tools and plan their safe use for a team of four.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with the drawing and job card, so I know the materials, sizes, number of parts and where the work will be done. I visit the site, or ask about it, to find the power supply (110 V or 220 V outlets, distance, RCD protection), the space, nearby flammable materials and whether students or the public will be around. I choose tools to suit each task: a cold saw or a grinder with a cutting disc for cutting, a magnetic base drill or pillar drill for the holes, and a grinder with a flap disc for blending. I check that each tool is tagged, in date and in good condition, and that we have the right discs, cutters and leads. I write a risk assessment covering electric shock, sparks and fire, flying particles, noise, dust and manual handling, with the controls, and arrange a hot work permit, screens and an extinguisher. I give each team member a clear task, check that each is trained on the tools they will use, and brief everyone before work starts.
markingPoints: Uses the drawing and job card to plan the work
Checks the site: supply voltage, RCD, space, fire risk, people nearby
Chooses a suitable tool for each task and checks tools and accessories
Writes a risk assessment with controls (permit, screens, extinguisher, PPE)
Allocates tasks to trained people and briefs the team

essays.stem: Describe the checks you would carry out on a corded power tool, its lead and the supply before use, and explain how the Centre's tagging and register system supports these checks.
essays.modelAnswer: I check that the tool's inspection tag is in date and that the tool is on the register. I look at the casing for cracks, and check that the guard, side handle and any other parts are fitted and secure. I check that the switch works freely and returns to off, and that the accessory (disc, bit or blade) is the right type and size and in good condition. I check the cable along its length for cuts, kinks, burns and bare wires, and that the outer sheath is held firmly where it enters the tool and the plug. I check that the plug is undamaged and that the voltage on the rating plate matches the outlet. Any extension lead gets the same checks and must be rated for the tool, and the supply must be RCD protected. The register and tags show when each tool was last inspected and tested by a competent person, and list repairs. A tool with a fault is tagged 'Do not use', recorded and taken out of use, so the next user can trust that a tagged, in-date tool is safe.
markingPoints: Checks tag and register
Checks casing, guard, handles, switch and accessory
Checks the cable, sheath grips and plug
Checks voltage, extension lead rating and RCD protection
Explains how tags and the register record checks, tests and faults

essays.stem: Explain how to choose, check and fit a disc to an angle grinder for (a) cutting a steel bar and (b) grinding a weld, and why the rated speed and size of the disc matter.
essays.modelAnswer: For cutting I choose a thin cutting disc, and for grinding a weld I choose a thicker grinding disc or a flap disc, both made for steel and the right diameter for the grinder. I check the disc's markings: its size, bore, maximum speed and any expiry date. The rated speed must be equal to or higher than the grinder's speed on its rating plate, because a disc spun faster than its rating can burst. A bigger disc than the grinder is made for also has a higher rim speed and cannot be guarded. I look for cracks, chips, damp or damage and do not use a damaged disc. I unplug the grinder, use the spindle lock, fit the correct flanges the right way round, fit the disc and tighten the nut with the key. I set the guard between the disc and me. I then stand to one side and run it for a short time before use, checking for wobble or vibration. I use a cutting disc only on its edge, never its side.
markingPoints: Chooses a cutting disc for cutting and a grinding or flap disc for weld grinding
Checks markings, condition and expiry; rated speed at least the grinder's speed
Explains why: overspeed or oversize discs can burst and cannot be guarded
Unplugs, uses spindle lock, correct flanges, tightens, sets the guard
Test run standing aside; cutting disc used only on its edge

essays.stem: Describe how to set up and use a magnetic base drill to cut a 22 mm hole in a steel beam safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the drill's tag, cable and switch, and choose a sharp 22 mm annular cutter with its pilot pin. I clean the beam where the drill will sit, removing paint, scale, swarf and grease, and check the steel is thick enough for the magnet to grip, as the maker's instructions say. I mark the hole centre and line up the pilot pin on the punch mark. I switch on the magnet and check it holds firmly, then fit the safety chain or strap around the beam, especially on a vertical or overhead face. I make sure no one is welding on the beam. I wear safety glasses, gloves suited to the task kept away from the cutter, and hearing protection, and keep loose clothing away. I fill the coolant bottle with cutting fluid. I start the motor, feed the cutter in gently at first, then with steady pressure, letting the swarf clear. After breakthrough I retract the cutter, switch off the motor, wait for it to stop, then switch off the magnet while holding the drill. I remove the slug and swarf with a hook, not my fingers.
markingPoints: Checks the drill and chooses the right cutter
Cleans the surface and checks the steel is suitable for the magnet
Lines up on the mark, sets the magnet, fits the safety chain; no welding on the beam
Wears PPE, uses cutting fluid, feeds steadily
Stops safely, holds the drill when releasing the magnet, clears swarf with a hook

essays.stem: Explain how the right drill speed is chosen. Use N = (1000 × V) ÷ (π × D) to work out the speeds for an 8 mm and a 20 mm HSS drill in mild steel at a cutting speed of 25 m/min, and say what happens if the speed is wrong.
essays.modelAnswer: The cutting speed V is how fast the edge of the drill moves past the metal, in metres per minute. It depends on the work material and the drill material; for HSS drills in mild steel about 25 m/min is often used, and it is lower for harder steels. The spindle speed N in rpm depends on the drill diameter D in millimetres, because a bigger drill's edge travels further each turn. For the 8 mm drill: N = (1000 × 25) ÷ (3.142 × 8) = 25 000 ÷ 25.1 = about 995 rpm. For the 20 mm drill: N = 25 000 ÷ (3.142 × 20) = 25 000 ÷ 62.8 = about 398 rpm. So the larger drill runs slower. I would set the nearest speed the machine has, below the figure. If the speed is too high, the drill overheats, the edges burn and go blunt, and stainless steel may work-harden. If it is too low, cutting is slow and the drill may chip or break from too much feed.
markingPoints: Explains cutting speed and that it depends on the materials
Explains that larger diameters need lower rpm
8 mm: about 995 rpm (working shown)
20 mm: about 398 rpm (working shown)
Effects of too high and too low a speed

essays.stem: Explain the main hazards of pneumatic (air-powered) tools and how each is controlled.
essays.modelAnswer: Compressed air is stored energy. A hose that comes apart can whip and strike people, so couplings are checked, whip checks are fitted across joints and hoses are kept in good condition. Air forced into the skin, eyes or ears can cause serious injury, so air is never pointed at anyone and never used to blow dust off clothes. Too much pressure can make a tool or accessory fail, so the regulator is set to the pressure the tool maker gives. A tool can start unexpectedly, so the air is shut off and the line bled before changing a cutter or clearing a jam, and the tool is disconnected. Air tools such as grinders and chisels are loud and vibrate, so hearing protection is worn and tasks are rotated. Flying particles call for safety glasses or a face shield. Hoses on the floor are a trip hazard, so they are routed along walls or overhead. The compressor and its receiver need regular checks and draining of water, as the maker's instructions say.
markingPoints: Hose whip: check couplings, use whip checks
Air injection: never point air at people or clean clothes with it
Correct pressure set at the regulator, as the maker says
Shut off, bleed and disconnect before changing accessories
Noise, vibration, flying particles and trip hazards controlled; compressor maintained

essays.stem: Explain the health hazards of noise, vibration and dust or fumes from power tools, and how a team leader controls them over a working week.
essays.modelAnswer: Loud tools such as grinders and needle scalers can damage hearing for good, and the damage builds up over time without pain. Long use of vibrating tools can cause hand-arm vibration syndrome, with numb, tingling or white fingers, pain and weak grip. Dust and fumes from grinding, cutting painted or galvanised steel and sanding can harm the lungs, and zinc fumes can cause fever-like illness. A team leader plans the week so that no one uses loud or vibrating tools all day: tasks are rotated and breaks taken. They choose low-noise and low-vibration tools, keep discs sharp and tools maintained, and use the right accessories, so that tools vibrate less and cut faster. Hearing protection is worn by everyone in the noisy area, and signs are put up. Dust and fumes are removed at source with extraction, the work is done in a well ventilated area, and suitable respirators are worn where needed. The leader also asks the team to report symptoms early, and records exposure times where the Centre requires it.
markingPoints: Noise: permanent hearing damage that builds up
Vibration: hand-arm vibration syndrome (numbness, white fingers)
Dust and fumes: lung harm, zinc fumes from galvanised steel
Controls: rotation, breaks, low-vibration tools, maintenance, hearing protection
Extraction, ventilation, respirators, reporting of symptoms and records

essays.stem: Describe the care, maintenance and storage of cordless power tools and their lithium-ion batteries.
essays.modelAnswer: Cordless tools are checked before use like any other tool: casing, guard, switch, chuck and accessory. The battery is taken out before changing a bit, blade or disc, and when the tool is put away, so that it cannot start by accident. Batteries are charged only on the maker's charger, on a hard surface in a cool, dry, ventilated place, away from anything that can burn, and not left charging unattended for long periods where the Centre's rules say so. They are not charged when very hot straight after heavy use. Batteries are kept clean and dry, and the terminals are protected so they cannot touch metal objects such as nails or coins, which could short them. A battery that is dropped hard, swollen, leaking, cracked or very hot is taken out of use, kept away from heat and flammables, reported and disposed of as the maker and the Centre say, not in the normal bin. Tools are wiped clean, vents brushed out and stored in their cases in a dry, locked store.
markingPoints: Pre-use checks; remove the battery before changing accessories and when storing
Charge only on the maker's charger in a cool, dry, safe place
Keep terminals clean and protected from metal objects
Damaged, swollen or hot batteries taken out of use and disposed of correctly
Clean and store tools dry and secure

essays.stem: Describe the routine care a user can carry out on power tools, what must be left to a competent repairer, and how faults should be reported and recorded.
essays.modelAnswer: A user can do the routine care in the maker's instructions. This includes keeping the tool clean, brushing or blowing out the air vents with eye protection worn, wiping off oil and dust, checking that screws, guards and handles are tight, changing discs, bits and blades, and keeping accessories sharp and stored dry. The user also does the visual checks before each use. Any work inside the tool or on its electrical parts must be left to a competent repairer, for example replacing a damaged cable or plug, carbon brushes, switches or bearings, and the electrical safety test after a repair. A user must never open the casing or bypass a guard or switch. When a fault is found, the tool is unplugged, tagged 'Do not use', taken out of service and handed in. The fault is written in the tool register or a fault report with the date, the tool's number, what is wrong and who found it. When the tool comes back, the repair and the test are recorded before it is used again.
markingPoints: User care: cleaning, vents, tightness checks, accessories, pre-use checks
Repairer only: cables, plugs, brushes, switches, internal parts, electrical tests
Never open casings or bypass guards and switches
Faulty tool unplugged, tagged and taken out of service
Fault, repair and test recorded in the register

essays.stem: A team member is injured when a grinder disc shatters. Describe what you would do at once, and what your incident report should contain to help stop it happening again.
essays.modelAnswer: First I make the area safe: switch off and unplug the grinder and keep others away. I check the injured person and give first aid, or call the first aider, and call for medical help if the injury is serious. I then leave the grinder, the pieces of the disc and the area as they are, as far as is safe, so they can be looked at, and tag the grinder out of use. I report the incident to the supervisor straight away. The report should give the date, time and place, the people involved and any witnesses, and what the person was doing. It should describe the injury and the first aid given. It should give the grinder's number, the disc type, size and rated speed, and whether the guard and side handle were fitted. It should give the likely cause, such as a disc rated below the grinder's speed, a damaged or damp disc, side loading of a cutting disc or a missing guard. Finally, it should suggest actions such as disc checks, training and a toolbox talk.
markingPoints: Makes the area safe and isolates the tool
Gives or gets first aid and medical help
Keeps the evidence and tags the tool; reports at once
Report: when, where, who, what happened, injury, tool and disc details
Likely cause and actions to prevent it happening again

practical1.title: Plan and make a batch of steel mounting brackets with power tools, with a risk assessment and tool check sheet
practical1.brief: As a team, plan and make six angle brackets from 50 × 50 × 6 mm steel angle to the drawing the assessor gives you (for example 100 mm long, with two 14 mm holes in each leg and the corners rounded). First, write a short plan and a risk assessment for the job: the tools for each step, the hazards and the controls. Check every power tool you will use and fill in the tool check sheet. Cut the angle to length with a cold saw, bandsaw or angle grinder, drill the holes with a magnetic base drill or pillar drill at the speed you have worked out, round the corners and remove burrs with a flap disc. The team leader role changes half way. Every member uses at least two different power tools while the assessor watches, and checks the brackets made by another member against the drawing. Record the checks on an inspection sheet. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the brackets are finished and the tools are cleaned, checked and stored.
materials: 50 × 50 × 6 mm steel angle, about 700 mm long
Drawing of the bracket (from the assessor)
Cold saw, bandsaw or 115/125 mm angle grinder with cutting discs
Magnetic base drill or pillar drill, 14 mm cutter or drill, cutting fluid
Angle grinder with flap disc; clamps; marking out tools
Plan, risk assessment, tool check sheet and inspection sheet
photos: The written plan, risk assessment and filled-in tool check sheet
A member checking a power tool, its cable and tag before use
Angle being cut to length, with the work clamped and PPE worn
Holes being drilled, with the drill secured and coolant in use
The six finished brackets laid out with the drawing
Tools cleaned and stored, and the completed inspection sheet
checklist: Helped write the plan and risk assessment and can explain the controls
Checked each power tool before use and recorded it
Chose and fitted the right disc, cutter or bit, with the power off
Held and guided each tool correctly, with guards and handles fitted
Clamped the work and worked out a suitable drill speed
Wore the right PPE (eye, face, hearing, hands) and kept others safe from sparks
Checked another member's brackets against the drawing and recorded it
Cleaned, checked and stored the tools, and reported any fault
safety: Check each tool's tag, cable, plug and guard; use RCD-protected outlets of the right voltage
Unplug or remove the battery before changing discs, bits or cutters
Clamp the work; never hold small parts by hand when drilling or cutting
Wear safety glasses, a face shield when grinding, hearing protection and gloves
Screen the area, remove anything that can burn and keep an extinguisher at hand
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Run an inspection and care session for the Centre's portable power tools, and deliver a toolbox talk
practical2.brief: As a team, plan and run an inspection and care session on at least eight of the Centre's portable power tools and leads that the assessor chooses (for example grinders, drills, a magnetic base drill, a cordless drill and an extension lead). Do visual inspections only: any electrical test is done by the Centre's competent person. For each tool, check the tag and register entry, casing, guard, handles, switch, accessory, cable, plug and, for cordless tools, the battery and charger. Clean each tool, brush out the vents and fit or change accessories as the maker's instructions say. Tag any faulty tool 'Do not use', fill in a fault report and update the register. Then plan and give a 10-minute toolbox talk to the class on one power tool hazard (for example grinder discs, kickback, or vibration), using one of the tools to show the points. Each member inspects at least two tools, and every member speaks in the toolbox talk. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the register, fault reports and talk notes are finished and the tools are stored.
materials: At least eight of the Centre's portable power tools and leads (unplugged)
The Centre's tool register, inspection tags and 'Do not use' tags
Inspection check sheets and fault report forms
Brushes, clean cloths and the maker's instructions for each tool
Spare discs, bits and accessories as needed
Flip chart or paper for the toolbox talk notes
photos: The plan for the session, with each member's tools
A member inspecting a tool's cable, plug and guard
A cordless battery and charger being checked
A faulty tool tagged 'Do not use', with its fault report
The updated register or inspection sheet
The team giving the toolbox talk, with the talk notes
checklist: Kept every tool unplugged or with its battery removed during the checks
Carried out a full visual inspection of each tool in a set order
Found and correctly recorded any faults, and tagged faulty tools
Cleaned the tools and fitted or changed accessories correctly
Updated the register and fault reports clearly and accurately
Spoke clearly in the toolbox talk and explained the hazard and its controls
Worked as a team and stored the tools correctly at the end
safety: Make sure every tool is unplugged, or its battery removed, before it is handled
Do not open any tool casing; electrical repairs and tests are for the competent person only
Wear safety glasses when brushing or blowing out vents
Keep swollen, leaking or damaged batteries away from heat and report them at once
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
